question: Does retaining a standard feed-forward activation while adding a compact trainable Fourier-feature residual behind a learnable, near-closed channel gate improve high-frequency expressivity, optimization stability, and accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision, language, audio, function fitting, and PDE tasks?

key_findings.claim: Author contribution: SGN adds an input-dependent, channel-wise gate over a projected trainable sine-cosine branch while leaving the standard activation pathway intact.
key_findings.evidence: For FFN pre-activation u, the target formulation is T(u)=phi(u)+G(u) times Psi_spec(u). The gate is a sigmoid of an elementwise affine transform of LayerNorm(u); the spectral path learns frequencies W_r, phases b_r, and projection A_r from 2m sine-cosine features back to d_ff. Unlike a pure basis replacement, setting the spectral projection small makes the initial forward map close to the base activation.

key_findings.claim: Author theorem with a material qualification: cold-start closeness follows from a small spectral projection, but the claimed small gradient for every spectral parameter also requires a separately near-closed gate.
key_findings.evidence: The appendix proves forward perturbation O(epsilon) from A_r=epsilon times a bounded matrix even with a generic gate. To make the gradient with respect to A_r itself O(epsilon), it additionally assumes the sigmoid gate is O(epsilon) for all initialization inputs through a sufficiently negative bias and small gate weight. This stronger condition is essential, and it simultaneously suppresses initial spectral learning signals.

key_findings.claim: Reviewer inference: the spectral-expansion proposition is a function-class containment result, not evidence that training finds high-frequency solutions or overcomes spectral bias.
key_findings.evidence: The appendix constructs a nearly constant open gate and chooses A_r so one output coordinate can contain arbitrary linear combinations of the selected sine and cosine bases. It explicitly narrows the claim to a lower bound on representable frequencies and disclaims estimator-dependent language. The construction does not analyze gradient dynamics, learned frequency placement, sample complexity, or whether the default input-dependent gate realizes the open-state construction.

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: two appendices describe different SGN parameterizations and incompatible parameter/FLOP counts.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix B counts a KAF-style layer with trainable RFF projection, two channel mixing vectors a and b, and one final linear projection, giving d_in M + M + 2d_in + d_in d_out + d_out parameters and about 4d_in M spectral FLOPs. Appendix I instead follows the main SGN equations and adds W_r, b_r, a separate 2m by d_ff projection A_r, and gate vectors, deriving roughly 3d_ff m parameters and 6d_ff m FLOPs of overhead. The paper never reconciles which implementation produced the reported 1.1x parameter and latency results.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported design ablation: an adaptive channel-wise spectral gate performs better than a fixed, additive, scalar, or fixed-frequency alternative in one CIFAR experiment.
key_findings.evidence: The design table reports 78.5 for a standard GELU FFN, 79.2 for spline KAN, 79.8 for pre-activation gating, 80.1 for post-mix gating, 81.5 for the selected spectral gate, 79.0 for scalar gating, 80.2 for fixed RFF, and 80.5 for an additive branch. Appendix Table 17 repeats 80.2 fixed gate, 80.5 no gate, and 81.5 adaptive gate. The architecture, split, run count, and uncertainty for this 81.5%-accuracy setting are not reported alongside the table.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported standard vision result: SGN improves each paired MLP baseline, but it is not the best listed method on two of four complex-backbone comparisons.
key_findings.evidence: SGN changes ResNet-18 CIFAR-10 from 91.19 to 91.72 with 11.1M to 12.0M parameters and 0.56G to 0.63G FLOPs; MLP-Mixer ImageNet-1K from 63.5 to 64.7 with 18.2M to 18.8M and 3.8G to 4.2G; ViT-Tiny ImageNet from 72.3 to 73.2; and MLP-KAN CIFAR-100 from 49.0 to 53.8. Yet GPKAN scores 74.6 on ViT-Tiny and 54.3 on MLP-KAN, above SGN's 73.2 and 53.8, contradicting unqualified claims that SGN consistently achieves the highest accuracy.

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: the headline optimized scores do not support a fair SGN-versus-MLP improvement because the corresponding optimized baseline cells are absent.
key_findings.evidence: Table 3 reports SGN Optimized at 93.15% for ResNet-18/CIFAR-10 and 79.3% for ViT-Tiny/ImageNet-1K, but marks MLP Optimized as TBD and also leaves SGN Standard as TBD. Although the prose says both MLP and SGN use the same optimized recipe and SGN continues to outperform the corresponding baseline, no optimized MLP number is supplied for either headline result.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported latency result: SGN is close to MLP and much faster than the selected spline KAN implementation at batch size one on an RTX 4090.
key_findings.evidence: For ResNet-18, Table 5 reports 3.4 ms/image for MLP, 3.6 for SGN, and 42.1 for KAN, yielding the stated 11.7x SGN-over-KAN speedup. For GPT-2, it reports 17.2 ms/token for MLP, 18.5 for SGN, and 145.3 for KAN, a 7.8x speedup. These are one-device batch-one measurements and the KAN language model elsewhere has 478M parameters versus 128M for SGN, so the latency ratio is not an architecture-only comparison.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported language result: replacing GPT-2's MLP with SGN substantially lowers reported perplexity with similar training time, while the much larger spline KAN fails to converge.
key_findings.evidence: On WikiText-103, the table gives MLP 37.50 PPL in 21h28m with 117M parameters, SGN 28.37 in 21h42m with 128M, and KAN 39,782 in 304h06m with 478M. On OpenWebText it gives 17.37 in 62h56m, 13.86 in 63h13m, and 27,832 in 960h19m. Dataset tokenization, token count, batch/sequence length, evaluation split, checkpoint selection, seeds, and uncertainty are not reported, so the large gain is not independently interpretable from the paper.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported retrofit result: zero-initialized SGN avoids an initial GPT-2 perplexity shock and can act as an 11M-parameter adapter, but its speed and significance claims are iteration-only and single-run.
key_findings.evidence: On WikiText-103, a standard MLP starts at 29.45 and ends at 19.24 after 20k steps; naive SGN starts at 582.4 and ends at 20.15 after more than 30k; zero-init full SGN starts at 29.46, ends at 18.41, and reaches the baseline endpoint at 12k; spectral-only SGN starts at 29.46 and ends at 19.05 with 11M trainable parameters. The claimed 1.6x speedup counts steps despite SGN's higher per-step cost, and 'statistically indistinguishable' is asserted without repeated-run statistics.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported function and PDE result: SGN is usually strong on plotted approximation errors, but the paper supplies too little protocol and numeric detail for the broad robustness conclusion.
key_findings.evidence: Eight synthetic functions and four PDEs are plotted against parameter count. The prose says SGN reaches about 1e-6 rather than 1e-5 error on selected high-frequency functions and is better or comparable across Poisson, wave, heat, and Burgers tasks. Most exact points, sample domains, train/test splits, collocation counts, boundary losses, widths, seeds, and error summaries are absent; the figures also show task-dependent winners rather than a uniform dominance result.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported negative result: Fourier-only extrapolation fails, and KAN is more robust than SGN to three of four tested noise regimes.
key_findings.evidence: For extrapolating x squared, the pure RFF-KAN test MSE is 1.1 versus 8.7e-3 for the MLP-labeled baseline and 9.1e-4 for hybrid SGN, motivating retention of a nonperiodic branch; train and extrapolation intervals are not given. In noise tests, KAN beats SGN under 10 dB Gaussian FNO (7.1e-3 versus 9.8e-3), 20 dB Gaussian PINN (5.2e-3 versus 6.7e-3), and 20% impulse FNO (8.9e-3 versus 1.1e-2); SGN is best only for the 30 dB high-frequency PINN case (5.5e-3 versus 5.8e-3).

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: the reported t-test section does not provide a valid reproducible significance analysis and mislabels at least one p-value under its own threshold.
key_findings.evidence: The methods text says multiple runs were 'assuming' to have been performed but gives no run count, per-run values, means, variances, independence argument, multiple-comparison correction, or test statistic. It defines significance as p<0.05, yet Table 11 labels the Bean KAN-versus-MLP p=0.06 result Significant, and the discussion repeats that claim; AG News p=0.05 is also called significant despite the stated strict inequality.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported hyperparameter sweep provides limited empirical support for sigma=1.64 but does not validate the theoretical derivation or the chosen frequency budget.
key_findings.evidence: On one CIFAR-10 maximum-test-accuracy sweep, sigma=1.64 gives the best listed 54.96%, narrowly above 1.8 at 54.68 and 1.7 at 54.64. For the quantity still called num_grids, the selected default 9 gives 54.96, but 20 gives a higher 55.01. No validation split, seeds, uncertainty, or correction for selecting maximum test accuracy over epochs and hyperparameters is provided.

key_findings.claim: Reviewer inference: the claimed Fourier-theoretic derivation of the GELU initialization constant is not mathematically established as written.
key_findings.evidence: The appendix treats an input 'x drawn from a Gaussian' as a deterministic signal, then writes ordinary Fourier integrals for x, the Gaussian CDF, and GELU over the real line even though x and GELU are not integrable there without a distributional treatment. It assumes a white target spectrum, quotes numerical integrals 0.168 and 0.062 without a reproducible integration protocol, and turns their ratio into 1.64. The later statement that the gate scale naturally grows to full spectral coverage is empirical rather than derived.

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: the broad architectural and empirical contribution substantially overlaps an uncited earlier paper from the same core author team.
key_findings.evidence: The target presents trainable random Fourier frequencies and phases, a hybrid GELU-Fourier path, progressive small-to-large spectral mixing, sigma=1.64, grid-independent complexity, and cross-domain KAN/MLP/FAN/GPKAN experiments as SGN contributions. Yet arXiv:2502.06018v1, posted one year earlier by Zhang, Fan, Cai, and Wang, already introduced KAF with those same elements, and its complex-vision table contains the exact 91.19/91.72, 72.3/73.2, 63.5/64.7, and 49.0/53.8 MLP/KAF results that this paper relabels MLP/SGN. SGN's narrower new element appears to be an input-dependent near-closed gate and its homotopy/retrofit treatment, but the paper does not cite or delineate KAF.

method.core_idea: Preserve a standard FFN's activation as a stable base and learn a gated residual composed of trainable sine-cosine features, so spectral capacity can be introduced gradually without the resolution-indexed spline tables and cold-start replacement of a KAN.
method.mechanism: The main formulation computes u=W1x+b1, keeps phi(u), maps u through learned frequencies and phases into m cosine plus m sine features, projects those 2m features back to d_ff, and multiplies them by a channel-wise sigmoid gate derived from LayerNorm(u) before adding the residual. Small spectral-projection weights and a negatively biased near-closed gate initialize the module close to the base MLP. The paper substitutes this operator into small classifiers, ResNet-18, ViT-Tiny, MLP-Mixer, an MLP-KAN backbone, and GPT-2, and also evaluates synthetic functions and PINN/FNO tasks. A separate retrofit freezes the pretrained MLP and trains only spectral and gate parameters.
assumptions: High-frequency components are a major limiting factor in the selected classification, language, audio, and PDE tasks rather than merely a useful additional parameterization.

A standard GELU branch can be interpreted as a stable low-frequency path and a learned Fourier branch as a high-frequency residual, although no branch-wise spectral decomposition is measured on the real tasks.
A fixed small frequency budget m is enough to capture task-relevant bands while remaining much smaller than d_ff.
Trainable RFF frequencies retain the kernel and spectral intuitions of random Fourier features after departing from their fixed random sampling regime.
A near-closed sigmoid gate and small projection preserve pretrained behavior without suppressing the spectral branch so strongly that it cannot learn.
Maximum test accuracy over epochs and hyperparameter choices is a fair architecture metric despite the absence of a reported validation-selection protocol.
Comparisons with KAN remain informative even when the KAN model has several times more parameters and fails to converge under the chosen implementation and schedule.
The parameter/FLOP accounting in the KAF-style appendix and the main SGN-style appendix describe the same evaluated implementation, despite their incompatible formulas.
The white-spectrum objective and ordinary Fourier-transform manipulations in the GELU analysis justify sigma=1.64 for diverse hidden-activation distributions.
Accuracy and perplexity differences from single reported runs reflect architecture effects rather than seed, recipe, data-processing, or checkpoint-selection differences.
A steeper line fitted to the displayed loss-versus-parameter points constitutes a general neural scaling law.
The exact results inherited from the earlier KAF paper remain valid evidence for the new input-dependent SGN gate.

techniques.role: Adds learned Fourier features to an unchanged base activation only after channel-wise sigmoid modulation.
Learns frequency vectors and phases rather than fixing a spline grid or a random input encoding.
Uses small spectral projection and a negative gate bias to make the initial operator and base gradients close to the original FFN.
Derives one bounded, input-dependent injection coefficient per hidden channel from normalized pre-activations.
Pairs cosine and sine at each learned frequency to represent phase-shifted periodic components.
Freezes pretrained GPT-2 MLP weights and tunes only the added frequency, projection, and gate parameters as an adapter.
Constructs an open-gate parameter setting to prove the function class contains the selected sinusoidal span.
Reports model size, FLOPs, batch-one latency, and training time against MLP and KAN variants.
Tests FNO/PINN variants under Gaussian, impulse, and Fourier-domain perturbations.
Compares adaptive channel gating with fixed, additive, scalar, and fixed-frequency spectral branches.

limitations: Reviewer-identified: the paper has no dedicated limitations section and makes broad consistency, scalability, and stability claims without a calibrated scope statement.

Reviewer-identified: it does not cite or distinguish the same-author KAF predecessor, which already contains the trainable RFF, GELU-Fourier hybrid, progressive scaling, sigma=1.64, cross-domain task suite, and exact complex-vision results.
Reviewer-identified: Appendix B uses a KAF-style two-scale formulation and different parameter/FLOP equations from the input-dependent SGN formulation proved in Appendix I.
Reviewer-identified: the headline 93.15% and 79.3% optimized results have no optimized MLP values; those cells are marked TBD.
Reviewer-identified: the standard complex-vision table shows GPKAN beating SGN on ViT/ImageNet and MLP-KAN/CIFAR-100 despite prose claiming consistent highest accuracy.
Reviewer-identified: experiments select and report maximum test accuracy and tune sigma and num_grids against test results without a described validation split, introducing test-selection leakage.
Reviewer-identified: most tables lack seed counts, error bars, data splits, optimizer schedules, augmentation details, and checkpoint-selection rules needed for reproduction.
Reviewer-identified: the t-tests state that multiple runs are assumed, omit the samples and test statistics, do not correct for multiple comparisons, and label p=0.06 significant under p<0.05.

Reviewer-identified: the GPT-2 results omit tokenizer, token count, sequence length, batch size, evaluation split, and seed information, and use inconsistent parameter totals and perplexity scales between the pretraining and retrofit sections.
Reviewer-identified: KAN latency and convergence comparisons are confounded by a 478M-parameter KAN versus 117M/128M MLP/SGN and no equally sized KAN control.

Reviewer-identified: the GELU Fourier transform and white-target-spectrum derivation of sigma=1.64 is not valid as an ordinary integrable-function calculation and is not connected to measured hidden spectra.
Reviewer-identified: spectral basis containment proves expressivity only, not optimization speed, frequency learning, generalization, or high-frequency fidelity.
Reviewer-identified: function-fitting and PDE plots omit enough exact settings and numbers that their broad cross-task claims cannot be independently reconstructed.
Reviewer-identified: the scaling-law claim is based on a small displayed parameter sweep with no fit uncertainty, held-out scale, or controlled compute/data scaling.
Reviewer-identified: the paper says code and trained models will be released but the target arXiv v1 provides no code URL, limiting verification of which of the two documented formulations was run.
Author-demonstrated: a pure Fourier/RFF model can extrapolate catastrophically on a nonperiodic trend, motivating the retained base branch.
Author-demonstrated: SGN is not uniformly most noise-robust; KAN wins three of four reported perturbation rows.
failure_modes: A gate initialized too open can destroy a pretrained representation, as the naive GPT-2 retrofit's initial perplexity spike demonstrates.
A gate initialized too closed together with a tiny spectral projection can starve every spectral parameter of gradient and delay useful frequency learning.
Learned frequencies can overfit periodic components, alias under discrete sampling, or extrapolate periodically when the target has an unbounded or nonperiodic trend.
Sin/cos evaluation and two dense spectral projections can cost materially more than claimed when m is not much smaller than d_ff.
An implementation following Appendix B rather than the main equations may evaluate KAF-style channel scales, not the claimed input-dependent SGN gate.
The RFF bandwidth constant tuned on one CIFAR setup may be badly mismatched to hidden-state distributions in language models, audio, or PDE solvers.
Input-dependent channel gates can saturate at zero or one, reducing adaptivity and creating poorly conditioned gradients.
High-frequency input noise can be amplified by a learned spectral path even when one selected Fourier-noise benchmark improves.
More parameters and test-set hyperparameter selection can create apparent accuracy gains that do not persist under equal-compute, validation-selected repeated runs.
Periodic features can represent sampled training points while behaving unpredictably between them or outside their sampled domain.
A spectral-only adapter may fail when adaptation requires changing attention, embeddings, or low-frequency base features rather than correcting an FFN residual.
reusable_insights: When augmenting a pretrained block, retain the original path exactly and initialize a residual branch near zero to separate expressivity from cold-start disruption.
Pair sine and cosine features so phase can be represented linearly, then learn frequency placement only if fixed-frequency ablations justify the extra instability.
Use an input-dependent bounded gate to localize a rich residual, but audit gate saturation and spectral-gradient magnitude throughout training.
Distinguish function-class expansion from trainability: containing high-frequency bases is not evidence that gradient descent will use them.
Report both per-step overhead and steps-to-target; fewer iterations alone is not a wall-clock speedup.
Include nonperiodic extrapolation and frequency-noise stress tests whenever sinusoidal features are added to a general-purpose network.
Compare accelerator-friendly basis expansions with splines at equal parameters as well as equal nominal layer role, because spline-table latency can otherwise be dominated by model-size mismatch.
Keep architecture equations, implementation code, parameter counts, and benchmark model sizes under one executable contract; divergent appendices can invalidate efficiency claims.
Audit novelty against same-team preprints and earlier versions before treating a reparameterized gate as an entirely new architecture.
open_questions: Which implementation produced the reported results: the KAF-style a/b mixing layer in Appendix B or the W_r/A_r/input-gate SGN layer in the main text and Appendix I?
After reproducing KAF and SGN under identical code, data, seeds, and parameter counts, what incremental gain comes specifically from the input-dependent gate?
Do the exact complex-vision results copied from the KAF paper change at all when the SGN gate replaces KAF's channel scales?
What are the optimized MLP baselines corresponding to 93.15% CIFAR-10 and 79.3% ImageNet, and do repeated-run intervals exclude parity?
How many runs generated each statistical test and noise standard deviation, and do corrected paired tests support the claimed differences?
Can sigma or the initial frequency distribution be selected from measured hidden-state spectra using a training-only validation protocol?
How quickly do gate values, A_r, and frequency gradients escape the near-zero homotopy regime layer by layer?
Does SGN improve calibrated robustness, corruption benchmarks, or out-of-distribution generalization beyond synthetic Fourier noise?
At matched parameters and optimized kernels, how does SGN compare with FAN, KAT, deep Fourier features, SwiGLU, and widened GELU MLPs?
Does the spectral-only adapter remain competitive with LoRA and standard adapter baselines at matched trainable parameters and wall-clock time?
Can a valid distributional Fourier analysis justify the 1.64 constant, or is it simply an empirical CIFAR hyperparameter?
What tokenizer, token budget, context length, batch size, and evaluation pipeline explain the very different perplexity scales in the two GPT-2 sections?
Does the method scale beyond GPT-2 Small when sin/cos kernels and extra projections are measured on modern LLM accelerators?
Can frequency learning be regularized to prevent aliasing, gate saturation, and nonperiodic extrapolation failure?

competitive_landscape.title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Fourier Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: same-author direct predecessor and novelty-critical overlap
competitive_landscape.difference: KAF v1, posted a year before SGN by Zhang, Fan, Cai, and Wang, already replaces spline bases with trainable RFF, combines them with GELU through progressive channel scales, derives the same sigma=1.64 initialization, evaluates the same vision/NLP/audio/function/PDE suite, and reports the exact complex-vision numbers relabeled in SGN. SGN's identifiable increment is an input-dependent sigmoid gate that leaves the base coefficient fixed, plus a homotopy proof and GPT retrofit experiment; the target neither cites KAF nor measures that incremental change directly.

competitive_landscape.title: FAN: Fourier Analysis Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: FAN is an accepted NeurIPS 2025 general-purpose MLP substitute that mixes learned periodic and nonperiodic components and evaluates symbolic functions, forecasting, language modeling, and image recognition with fewer parameters/FLOPs. SGN keeps the exact GELU base and uses an explicit bounded residual gate and trainable RFF projection, which offers a clearer warm-start path, but the target's own standard table does not uniformly beat FAN or other alternatives under a complete repeated-run protocol.

competitive_landscape.title: Plastic Learning with Deep Fourier Features
competitive_landscape.difference: Deep Fourier Features already concatenate sine and cosine in every hidden layer as a drop-in activation replacement and demonstrate sustained trainability across continual CIFAR and tiny-ImageNet settings. SGN instead preserves a GELU path, learns frequency vectors, and gates a projected spectral residual, targeting static cross-domain accuracy and pretrained retrofits; it does not compare against this prior on trainability, regularization, or continual learning.

competitive_landscape.title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Transformer
competitive_landscape.difference: KAT addresses spline GPU cost and initialization by replacing B-splines with rational functions, sharing activation parameters in groups, using variance-preserving initialization, and supplying CUDA kernels. SGN uses global sine-cosine features and a residual gate rather than rational grouped activations. The target compares mainly with a large pykan spline model, not the more deployment-relevant KAT design, so its claim to be the only viable scalable basis-augmented alternative is too broad.

competitive_landscape.title: KAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: KAN learns a univariate spline on every edge and emphasizes accuracy, scaling, and interpretability for compact scientific models. SGN gives up that explicit edge-function representation for dense global Fourier features, MLP-like accelerator operations, and warm-start compatibility. Its large-backbone efficiency advantage is plausible, but the reported KAN failures use an unmatched 478M-parameter language model and do not test optimized grouped/rational KAN implementations.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims a new drop-in spectral FFN reparameterization whose compact trainable RFF branch, adaptive gate, stable base path, and hybrid GELU-Fourier design resolve the spectral-expressivity versus efficiency trade-off across modalities.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The main equations introduce an input-dependent channel gate and the appendix proves forward and base-gradient closeness under small-projection initialization, with the stronger near-closed-gate assumption needed for all spectral gradients. Ablations favor the adaptive gate over fixed and additive variants, and one GPT-2 retrofit reports no initialization shock.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Broad architectural novelty is contradicted by the same-team KAF preprint arXiv:2502.06018v1, which predates SGN and already contains trainable RFF, a GELU-Fourier hybrid, progressive small spectral mixing, sigma=1.64, grid-independent efficiency, the same task suite, and exact benchmark numbers reused here. The narrow potentially new contribution is replacing KAF's input-independent channel scales with an input-dependent near-closed sigmoid residual gate, then formalizing cold-start closeness and testing a spectral-only retrofit. That increment is not cleanly isolated against KAF, and divergent KAF-style versus SGN-style appendix equations make it unclear which module generated the results. The empirical evidence therefore supports a promising gated variant requiring reproduction, not the claimed first general spectral reparameterization or established cross-domain dominance.

reviewer_notes: Primary full-text review of all 31 extracted pages, including theoretical appendices A-I, every displayed table, and references. Local PDF/text SHA-256 values were recomputed and match the fulltext index; all 31 pages have usable extracted text. arXiv currently lists the target only as arXiv:2602.07679v1, checked 2026-08-23. The novelty audit compared both the current KAF v3 primary record and the timestamped KAF v1 PDF, which establishes that the core same-author method and exact complex-vision table predate SGN. FAN, Deep Fourier Features, KAT, and KAN titles and current arXiv versions were also checked directly on 2026-08-23. Confidence is high in the reading and internal contradiction audit, not in the unreproduced benchmark claims. This is a first-pass full_text reading and has not been promoted to secondary verified status.
